seed_groups.title: Candidate Fixes / Design Directions
seeds: Clarify first Orchestrator seam in scope: UI/IA, execution model/state machine, lineage/receipts, or recovery/rollback/blocked behavior.
Capture terminology, precedence, effective-vs-requested state, and ownership in ledger as decisions emerge.
Treat Orchestrator as projection/control surface over canonical runtime contracts.
Keep scheduler semantics, attempt identity, blocked reasons, actions, and remediation lineage in shared runtime docs.
Let Orchestrator page own tabs, control affordances, and projection composition.
Define canonical facts vs orchestrator projections vs widget/page presentation boundary.
Distinguish requested vs effective state wherever provider/model/persona fallback occurs.
Node graph is already source for scheduling/execution inputs.
Open question: tiers as presentation/grouping only vs independently meaningful orchestration layer.
Prefer deterministic scheduler/state machine orchestrator over monolithic long-running super-agent.
Dispatch bounded worker/reviewer/remediation agents with explicit context windows and attempt IDs.
Allow lightweight planning/replan agent only at graph construction/patch boundaries.
Governance model: run=canonical graph; work package=coherent subgraph with local overseer; feature seam=cross-package oversight scope; node=smallest unit.
Overseers can challenge package outcomes; newly discovered work must become remediation nodes or graph-patch requests.
Use quorum/corroboration agents before accepting high-impact overseer challenges.
Seam completion requires integration quality, not package-local pass status only.
Promotion classes: lane_to_package, package_to_seam_available, seam_complete.
Promotions should be explicit runtime transitions, not implicit side effects.
Maintain automation-first defaults with optional HITL pause boundaries.
Surface blocked/HITL/critical promotion states on Dashboard, Orchestrator, and spawned chat thread.
lane_to_package gates: local correctness, uncontaminated lane state, required automated verification/review, promotable outputs.
package_to_seam_available gates: trusted package baseline, package evidence, acceptable overseer verdict, seam-consumable outputs.
seam_complete gates: integration review, no unresolved major/critical findings, seam evidence, workflow completeness, GUI/runtime alignment, no pending corroboration/remediation.
Next requested subtopic: required evidence at node/package/seam levels for concrete promotion gates.
Execution settings likely need provider/model defaults or overrides at run, seam, package, node, package overseer, seam overseer, and overseer-delegated node worker levels.
Show requested vs effective provider/model at every level where fallback/override can occur.
Node persona should default dynamically from node scope/type.
Node persona override should be node-worker policy, not per-node manual config.
Seam/package/node each need independent provider/model/effort configuration surfaces.
Overseer personas should be explicit settings-owned roles.
Node worker personas/provider/model remain overrideable.
Settings should define whether overseers may delegate node work to subagents and provider/model policy for delegates.

Suggested discussion order: orchestrator ownership boundaries -> tab responsibilities/CTAs -> cross-links (Usage/Evidence/Graph/history/blocked outcomes) -> provider/model/persona precedence -> worktree ownership/isolation.
